papers.title: Small molecule structure elucidation from NMR spectra with generative and reasoning models.
papers.abstract: Elucidating the structures of unknown small molecules remains a major challenge in chemistry, pharmacology, and drug discovery. While nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is the gold standard for structure elucidation, interpreting spectra remains labor-intensive and requires expert knowledge to navigate the vast space of possible structures. Here, we present an AI system for rapid, automated de novo structure elucidation that combines a molecular generative model with a scientific reasoning agent. Its generative component, ChefNMR2, is an atomic flow-matching model that predicts smal
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces an AI system that combines a generative flow-matching model (ChefNMR2) with a scientific reasoning agent to automatically determine the chemical structures of unknown small molecules from NMR spectra. The approach aims to replace labor-intensive expert spectral interpretation by navigating the vast space of possible structures computationally. It represents a step toward fully automated de novo structure elucidation in chemistry and drug discovery.

papers.title: MultiTargetDB: a comprehensive database of multitarget ligands for polypharmacology research and drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Multitarget drug discovery has gained considerable traction in recent years, particularly for the treatment of complex diseases. Despite the growing demand for dedicated, well-curated resources to advance polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery, such resources remain severely limited. Here, we present MultiTargetDB, a database of multitarget ligands integrated with comprehensive biological annotations and measurement-level provenance. At the small molecule level, MultiTargetDB integrates chemical structures (including molecular scaffolds), their drug development stage
papers.summary: MultiTargetDB is a new database that curates multitarget ligands—small molecules that bind multiple biological targets—along with detailed biological annotations and measurement-level provenance. It integrates chemical structures, molecular scaffolds, and drug development stages to support polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery. This fills a gap in dedicated, well-curated resources for multitarget drug discovery.

papers.title: Computational network pharmacology and molecular simulations to explore the potential mechanisms of Pyrrosia piloselloides compounds against prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality in men worldwide. Emerging evidence highlights the dragon scale fern (Pyrrosia piloselloides or P. piloselloides) has demonstrated anticancer potential, but its molecular mechanisms against prostate cancer remain unclear. The study aimed to investigate its potential anticancer compounds and underlying molecular mechanisms using an integrated in silico approach.
papers.journal: Journal of the Egyptian National Cancer Institute
papers.summary: This study uses computational network pharmacology and molecular dynamics simulations to predict which compounds from the dragon scale fern (Pyrrosia piloselloides) might act against prostate cancer and through which molecular targets. The work is entirely in silico, so it generates hypotheses about candidate compounds and pathways rather than experimental validation. It provides a starting point for follow-up wet-lab testing of this plant's anticancer potential.

papers.title: From LC-MS Metabolomic Profiling to AIEnabled Navigation of NPs Chemical Space: Recent Advances and Emerging Directions.
papers.abstract: Natural products (NPs) occupy a unique region of chemical space and continue to provide privileged scaffolds for drug discovery, chemical ecology, and biotechnology. However, the exploration of NP diversity remains constrained by the complexity of biological extracts, the low annotation rate of LC-MS features, and the rediscovery of known metabolites. Recent advances in LC-HRMS/MS-based metabolomics, coupled with expanding spectral and structural databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation methods, have considerably improved the characterization of complex metabolomes and facilit
papers.summary: This review surveys how LC-MS metabolomic profiling, expanding spectral and structural databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation are improving characterization of complex natural product extracts. It highlights how AI-enabled approaches can help navigate natural product chemical space and address persistent bottlenecks such as low annotation rates and rediscovery of known metabolites.

papers.title: Modeling ethnic differences via drug-predicted clearance from chemical structures.
papers.abstract: Ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics can result in clinically relevant differences in drug efficacy and safety, even when identical doses are administered. Although mechanistic approaches such as physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling can be used to evaluate population-specific pharmacokinetics, there remains a need for complementary screening approaches that can assess ethnic difference risk at very early stages of drug discovery with limited experimental information. The aim of this study was to develop a machine-learning-based approach to assess the risk of ethnic differences in o
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: The authors developed a machine-learning approach that predicts drug clearance directly from chemical structures to screen for potential ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics early in drug discovery. This offers a complementary, low-data screening tool alongside mechanistic methods like PBPK modeling.

papers.title: Structure-function relationships in a square-planar Cu(ii) hybrid halometalate: experimental, DFT, molecular docking, optical, and biological studies.
papers.abstract: A novel organic-inorganic copper(ii) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], was successfully synthesized and investigated using complementary experimental and computational approaches. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2- anions embedded within a three-dimensional supramolecular architecture stabilized by N-H⋯Br hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking interactions, and halogen contacts. Optical studies indicated semiconducting characteristics with an estimated band gap of approximately 2.5 eV, together with a broad visible emission assigned to ligand-to-me
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a new organic-inorganic copper(II) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], and characterized its crystal structure, which features discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2- anions held together by hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking, and halogen contacts. Optical measurements show semiconducting behavior with a ~2.5 eV band gap and broad visible emission, and the work is complemented by DFT, molecular docking, and biological assays. The study links the material's structure to its optical and biological properties.

papers.title: In Silico Investigation of Candidate Anticancer Targets for Aryltetralin Lignans Previously Reported from Cleistanthus Species.
papers.abstract: Aryltetralin lignans isolated from the fruits of Cleistanthus species exhibit substantial cytotoxic activity, although the molecular interactions underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. This study combined computational target investigation with previously published experimental chemical characterization and cytotoxic evidence and no new isolation or cytotoxicity experiments were carried out. Cleistantoxin, 7-hydroxypicropolygamain, neo-cleistantoxin, cleisindoside A, cleisindoside D, and cleistonkinin D were previously isolated from C. indochinensis, C. tonkinensis, C. eberha
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and target-prediction approaches to investigate which proteins might mediate the anticancer (cytotoxic) effects of six aryltetralin lignans previously isolated from Cleistanthus plants. No new experiments were performed; the work integrates prior chemical and cytotoxicity data with in silico target identification. The findings propose candidate molecular targets that could guide future experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrating Multisource Target Evidence with Machine-Learning Potency Prediction for Alzheimer's Disease Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) target evidence is distributed across biological, chemical, structural, regulatory, and trial-registry sources, complicating reproducible target evaluation and modeling. We developed a traceable data-to-model platform that integrates AGORA-centered evidence through Target Explorer, Drug-Target Lookup, and Model Portfolio workspaces. The resource contains 967 targets, 452,249 compounds, and 1,430,260 measurements. On a curated PIK3CA dataset, target-specific fine-tuning of the Boltz-2 affinity head increased Pearson r from 0.248 to 0.560 and reduced mean absolute error
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors built a traceable data-to-model platform for Alzheimer's disease drug discovery that integrates target evidence from biological, chemical, structural, regulatory, and trial-registry sources, covering 967 targets, 452,249 compounds, and 1,430,260 measurements. As a proof of concept, target-specific fine-tuning of the Boltz-2 affinity head on a curated PIK3CA dataset improved potency prediction (Pearson r from 0.248 to 0.560) and reduced mean absolute error.

papers.title: Advancing CD38 from a marker of disease activity to an active regulator of interferon responses in juvenile dermatomyositis.
papers.abstract: Juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM), the most common pediatric inflammatory myopathy, is driven by an overactive immune signaling pathway called type I interferon. Current treatment relies on broadly immunosuppressive agents that lack mechanistic specificity, often fail to achieve durable disease control, and can result in off-target toxicity and irreversible disease-related damage in many patients. CD38, a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+)-consuming ectoenzyme with known roles in immune cell metabolism, is elevated in JDM, but whether CD38 marks disease activity or plays a causal role in di
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates whether CD38, an NAD+-consuming enzyme elevated in juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM), is merely a marker of disease activity or an active driver of the type I interferon pathway that underlies the disease. The work aims to clarify CD38's mechanistic role, potentially informing more targeted therapies than current broad immunosuppression. The abstract is truncated, so the specific causal findings are not fully stated.

papers.title: Computational Identification of GABA-A Receptor Ligands Targeting the Histamine Allosteric Pocket.
papers.abstract: The γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABA-A) receptor is a key regulator of inhibitory neurotransmission in the central nervous system, and a promising target for cognitive and neurological disorders. Histamine interacts with a distinct allosteric pocket located at the β3-β3 subunit interface, providing an opportunity for the discovery of novel ligands. In the present study, an integrated in silico workflow combining ligand-based similarity analysis, ADMET filtering, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations was applied to identify candidate ligands for this histamine-associated site. D
papers.summary: This study used a computational pipeline—ligand similarity screening, ADMET filtering, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations—to identify candidate small molecules that bind the histamine allosteric pocket at the β3-β3 interface of the GABA-A receptor. The work proposes novel in silico ligand candidates for this site, which could inform future drug discovery for cognitive and neurological disorders, though experimental validation is not reported.

papers.title: Navigating the Eukaryotic Paradox: Insights for AI-Driven Computational Strategies Against Antifungal Resistance.
papers.abstract: The escalating crisis of invasive fungal infections and increasing antifungal resistance demand rapid therapeutic innovation. Given the critically narrow clinical arsenal, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as pivotal strategies to accelerate drug repurposing, providing a rapid alternative to de novo drug discovery. However, translational success in medical mycology faces a major biological hurdle: the "eukaryotic paradox," the extensive genomic, metabolic, and structural homology between fungal cells and human hosts. This review provides a critical and compara
papers.summary: This review examines how the 'eukaryotic paradox'—the extensive genomic, metabolic, and structural similarity between fungal pathogens and human hosts—complicates AI/ML-driven drug repurposing efforts against antifungal resistance. It critically compares computational strategies and highlights how host-pathogen homology creates challenges for target selectivity and toxicity prediction, offering guidance for more effective AI-driven therapeutic discovery in medical mycology.

papers.title: Network-enabled drug repurposing identifies lithium to promote cardiomyocyte proliferation.
papers.abstract: The adult mammalian heart has minimal regenerative capacity, limited in part by endogenous cardiomyocyte (CM) renewal. Although CM proliferation is a promising target in both congenital and adult heart disease, no current therapies specifically target this process. Progress has been hindered by the complexity of CM proliferation signaling networks, which may require systems-level approaches. The overall goal of this study was to leverage systems modeling to identify FDA approved drugs that have the potential to be repurposed towards CM proliferation. To achieve this goal, we developed a comput
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used a computational network model of cardiomyocyte proliferation signaling to identify FDA-approved drugs that could be repurposed to stimulate heart muscle cell renewal. The analysis pinpointed lithium as a candidate, which the authors then tested and found promotes cardiomyocyte proliferation. The work demonstrates how systems-level drug repurposing can uncover new therapeutic strategies for cardiac regeneration.

papers.title: QSAR-Guided In Silico Design of Piperazinylanthranilamide Factor Xa Inhibitors: Applicability-Domain Assessment, ADMET Profiling, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, and MM/GBSA.
papers.abstract: An integrated computational workflow was developed to prioritize piperazinylanthranilamide factor Xa (FXa) inhibitor candidates. Twenty literature compounds were geometry-optimized and described using alvaDesc to construct a constrained additive multivariate adaptive regression splines model. Internal validation and an assessment of the applicability domain guided the evaluation of 20 prospective analogs. Ten selected analogs and two same-series references were docked to FXa, with apixaban as the crystallographic comparator. Thirteen initial 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were supplemen
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated computational workflow—QSAR modeling, applicability-domain assessment, ADMET profiling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and MM/GBSA—to prioritize piperazinylanthranilamide analogs as factor Xa inhibitors. Twenty literature compounds were used to build a constrained MARS model, which guided the selection of ten prospective analogs for docking and simulation against apixaban. The work demonstrates a rational in silico pipeline for early-stage anticoagulant candidate triage.

papers.title: Donor-Resolved Analysis of HES1-Associated Fibroblast States in Systemic Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc) and the rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat. Methods: We analysed 325,636 skin cells from 230 donors across five non-redundant cohorts using complete computational transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data and spatial assays. Donors or independent simulations were the inference units, with cohort adjustment and multiplicity correction where applicable. Three independent 200 ns molecular dynamics runs per condition c
papers.summary: This study analyzed over 325,000 skin cells from 230 donors across five cohorts to characterize HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc). Using transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data, and spatial assays, the authors provide a rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat as a therapeutic strategy. The work emphasizes donor-resolved inference to identify fibroblast states linked to HES1 activity in SSc skin.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology of Natural Products from Computational Prediction to Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Natural products are important sources of bioactive compounds, but their complex chemical composition and multi-target effects make their mechanisms difficult to investigate using conventional approaches. Network pharmacology provides a systems-level framework for integrating chemical, biological, and disease-related information to investigate these complex interactions. This review describes the network pharmacology workflow, from active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation and target prediction to network construction and pathway enrichment, and the complementary roles of molecular docking a
papers.summary: This review outlines the network pharmacology workflow for studying natural products, covering active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation, target prediction, network construction, and pathway enrichment, along with the complementary roles of molecular docking and experimental validation. It provides a systems-level framework for investigating the multi-target mechanisms of complex natural product mixtures.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Virtual Screening Identifies a Novel MELK-Targeted Antiproliferative Lead Compound with G2/M Arrest Activity in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer and Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells.
papers.abstract: Background: Maternal embryonic leucine zipper kinase (MELK) is a cell cycle-regulated serine/threonine kinase frequently overexpressed in human malignancies, and represents a promising anticancer drug target. Discovery of structurally novel, highly selective MELK inhibitors remains an unmet need. Methods: In the study, we implemented an integrated computational pipeline combining four machine learning regressors (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM), hierarchical Glide docking (HTVS to SP to XP), MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations to
papers.summary: This study used a machine learning-guided virtual screening pipeline—combining four ML regressors, hierarchical molecular docking, MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations—to identify a novel MELK kinase inhibitor. The lead compound showed antiproliferative activity and G2/M cell cycle arrest in triple-negative breast cancer and lung adenocarcinoma cell lines. It represents a proof-of-concept for integrating ML with structure-based screening to discover new anticancer drug leads.

papers.title: In Silico Discovery of a Potential PI3Kα Inhibitor Incorporating an Imidazole Moiety for Breast Cancer Treatment.
papers.abstract: Excessive activation of PI3Kα is prevalent in breast cancer, aberrantly activating the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway to drive tumor progression, thus rendering PI3Kα a vital therapeutic target. Two PI3Kα inhibitors (alpelisib and inavolisib) have been approved for clinical application. Inavolisib exerts a mutation-selective degradation mechanism and functions by directly eliminating aberrant proteins. To develop novel PI3Kα inhibitors, we employed multiple computational strategies including scaffold hopping based on the structure of inavolisib, -CDOCKER docking, Lipinski's rule of five, ADMET predicti
papers.summary: The authors used computational methods—scaffold hopping from the approved PI3Kα inhibitor inavolisib, molecular docking, drug-likeness filtering, and ADMET prediction—to identify a novel imidazole-containing compound as a candidate PI3Kα inhibitor for breast cancer. This is a purely in silico study with no experimental validation reported, so the compound remains a hypothesis requiring wet-lab testing.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics-Guided Triage of Approved Drugs Against Escherichia coli Resistance Targets Nominates Capmatinib, Metergoline and Nilotinib as Candidates for Experimental Testing.
papers.abstract: Virtual screening ranks compounds by scoring functions that correlate with molecular size, and hit lists are rarely benchmarked against compounds of established activity. We screened 2070 approved drugs against four Escherichia coli targets selected by pocket-druggability triage (FabI, LpxC, DHFR and GyrB), with each docking protocol validated by redocking its native ligand (RMSD 0.50-0.69 Å). Per target, the two top-scoring compounds and a reference inhibitor were simulated for 100 ns in triplicate (12 complexes, 3.6 μs). Docking did not recover the references: trimethoprim ranked 762/2068 an
papers.summary: The authors docked 2070 approved drugs against four E. coli antibacterial targets (FabI, LpxC, DHFR, GyrB) and then ran 100 ns triplicate molecular dynamics simulations on top hits plus reference inhibitors. Docking failed to recover known reference inhibitors (e.g., trimethoprim ranked 762/2068 for DHFR), highlighting the limits of scoring functions, but MD-based triage nominated capmatinib, metergoline, and nilotinib as candidates for experimental testing. The work is a computational repurposing screen whose hits remain untested.

papers.title: DockBind: A Quality-Controlled Data Set of Modeled Protein-Ligand Complexes Associated with Affinity Data.
papers.abstract: Ligand-protein interaction prediction is essential for structure-based drug discovery, but further development of machine-learning scoring functions is limited by a lack of high-quality training data sets. Here, we present DockBind, a curated data set of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, generated through a quality-controlled docking workflow. This workflow was developed based on an expanded docking benchmark, where we systematically evaluated free and template-based docking methods as well as ligand similarity and maximum common substructure (MCS
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: DockBind is a curated dataset of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, created through a quality-controlled docking workflow. The authors built an expanded docking benchmark to systematically evaluate free and template-based docking methods, as well as ligand similarity and maximum common substructure approaches, to ensure data quality. This resource aims to address the shortage of high-quality training data for machine-learning scoring functions in structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Bioinformatics analyses were conducted using publicly available HCC transcriptomic datasets from GEO database, disease gene database (GeneCards database), and chemical-gene interaction networks (Comparative Toxicogenomic Database) to identify potential therapeutic targets, HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key therapeutic ta
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics analysis of public HCC transcriptomic and chemical-gene interaction data to identify HDAC2 and HDAC6 as targets of sodium propionate, a short-chain fatty acid. In vitro experiments in hepatocellular carcinoma cells then show that sodium propionate has anticancer activity associated with downregulation of these two histone deacetylases. The work suggests a potential epigenetic therapeutic role for this dietary/metabolite compound in liver cancer.

papers.title: Strengthening Japan's drug discovery and medical research ecosystem: AMED's innovation challenge.
papers.abstract: Japan continues to face challenges in translating life science and medical research into innovative medicines and healthcare technologies. The Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development (AMED), established in 2015, plays a central role in bridging basic research and practical application. To address gaps between research and development stages and to promote practical application of promising technological seeds from academia, AMED adopted five strategic priorities under its Third Mid- to Long-Term Plan (2025-2029). (1) Strengthen coordination across AMED programs to ensure seamless sup
papers.summary: This commentary describes how AMED, Japan's main medical research funding agency established in 2015, is restructuring its programs to better bridge basic research and clinical application. Under its Third Mid- to Long-Term Plan (2025-2029), AMED has adopted five strategic priorities aimed at closing gaps between R&D stages and moving promising academic discoveries toward practical use.

papers.title: An educational activity tailored for undergraduate students on AI-driven nanobody design for targeted antiviral therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Protein-based biologics are converging at an unprecedented pace as generative artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes early-stage drug discovery. Nanobodies, single-domain antibody fragments derived from camelid heavy chain-only immunoglobulins, are an emerging class of antiviral biologics prized for their small size, stability, and access to cryptic viral epitopes. Traditional nanobody discovery relies on animal immunization and phage display screening, a process that can take 6 to 12 months and is entirely inaccessible within a standard undergraduate laboratory session. Here, we describe a suc
papers.summary: This paper describes a short educational activity that teaches undergraduate students how to use generative AI tools to design nanobodies against viral targets, replacing the months-long traditional workflow of animal immunization and phage display with a computational exercise. The activity aims to make cutting-edge AI-driven biologics design accessible within a standard lab session, giving students hands-on exposure to modern drug discovery methods.

papers.title: Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches.
papers.abstract: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a key therapeutic target for various cancers because of its central role in tumor growth and survival signaling. This study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, umbrella sampling (US), and toxicity prediction to identify potential ALK inhibitors from 307 phytochemicals of the Glycosmis genus. A previously validated CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies, leading to the selection of 26 compounds with ΔG ML < -11 kcal mol-1. Molecular docking id
papers.summary: This study used a computational pipeline combining machine learning, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and umbrella sampling to screen 307 phytochemicals from the Glycosmis genus for potential inhibitors of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK), a cancer drug target. A CatBoost model predicted binding free energies and identified 26 compounds with strong predicted affinity, which were then validated through docking and simulation approaches. The work proposes candidate natural-product ALK inhibitors for further experimental testing.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and docking analysis of benzene sulfonamide-[1,4]benzoxazepine hybrids as acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitors.
papers.abstract: A series of novel hybrid [1,4]benzoxazepine-based sulfonamide derivatives 9-12a-j were synthesized and evaluated for their inhibitory activity against acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE). Compounds 9a and 9b exhibited potent dual cholinesterase inhibition, with IC50 values of 9.04 and 8.61 µM against AChE and 3.08 and 4.64 µM against BChE, respectively. Compound 12j emerged as the most potent BChE inhibitor of the series (IC50 = 1.06 ± 0.11 µM), displaying pronounced BChE preference (SI = 10.37), whereas 9d showed the highest BChE selectivity (BChE IC50 = 4.18 ± 0.56 µ
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of hybrid [1,4]benzoxazepine-sulfonamide compounds and tested them as inhibitors of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), enzymes relevant to Alzheimer's disease. Several compounds showed micromolar dual inhibition, with compound 12j being the most potent BChE inhibitor (IC50 ~1 µM) and 9d showing the highest BChE selectivity. Docking analysis was used to rationalize binding.

papers.title: Innovative design and development of novel thiazole-paracetamol hybrids as COX inhibitors and immunomodulatory activity: design, synthesis, SAR, in vitro biological evaluation, and molecular docking analysis.
papers.abstract: The hybridization approach was employed to design a single pharmacophore based on the conjugation of paracetamol with thiazole derivatives, yielding thiazole-paracetamol hybrid derivatives 4-11 that utilize a linker from hydrazone (-C[double bond, length as m-dash]N-NH) and azo (-N[double bond, length as m-dash]N-) linkers, serving as the hydrogen bond donor/acceptor binding site. The structure of the designed derivatives was fully characterized and confirmed using analytical data (IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR), and elemental analysis. The anti-inflammatory potential of the synthesized hybrids was
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of hybrid molecules combining paracetamol with thiazole derivatives via hydrazone or azo linkers, aiming to create dual-acting COX inhibitors with immunomodulatory activity. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically and evaluated in vitro for anti-inflammatory potential, with structure-activity relationships and molecular docking supporting the design rationale.

papers.title: Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction by Integrating Deep Learning Representations with Chemical Compound Knowledge.
papers.abstract: Predicting blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability is essential for central nervous system drug discovery, but traditional descriptor-based methods of predicting BBB permeability lack structural context, and deep learning-based methods struggle with overfitting. We introduce a multimodel framework that integrates both transformer-derived molecular embeddings with physicochemical descriptors using a late-stage ensemble fusion strategy. Trained on both the B3DB and NeuTox data sets and evaluated on the benchmark BBBP, our model showed strong predictive performance, with data set-dependent perform
papers.summary: This paper presents a hybrid machine learning framework for predicting blood-brain barrier permeability by combining transformer-derived molecular embeddings with traditional physicochemical descriptors using late-stage ensemble fusion. Trained on B3DB and NeuTox datasets and evaluated on the BBBP benchmark, the model aims to overcome limitations of descriptor-only methods (lack of structural context) and pure deep learning approaches (overfitting). The approach shows strong predictive performance, though results are dataset-dependent.

papers.title: Design, click synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors: antiproliferative activity, mechanistic insights, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: A novel series of uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids was designed, synthesized, and evaluated as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors to target cancer cell proliferation and survival. Synthesis was initiated via the nucleophilic substitution of 2-chloro-N-(1,3-dimethyl-2,6-dioxo-pyrimidin-4-yl)acetamide (3) with sodium azide, yielding the key intermediate 4. Subsequent copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloadditions (CuAAC) with various terminal alkynes and 1,3-dicarbonyls afforded the target triazole analogues 6a,b, 8a-c, and 10b,c. In vitro antiproliferative screening against a panel of four human cancer cell
papers.summary: The authors designed and synthesized a series of uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrid compounds using click chemistry (CuAAC) and screened them for anticancer activity, aiming to inhibit both EGFR and CDK1 simultaneously. The compounds showed antiproliferative effects against several human cancer cell lines, with mechanistic and computational (in silico) studies supporting dual-target binding. This is an early-stage medicinal chemistry effort identifying a new scaffold for potential cancer therapy.

papers.title: Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.
papers.abstract: Repurposing approved drugs offers a time- and cost-effective alternative to traditional drug development. However, in silico prediction of repurposing candidates is challenging and requires the effective collaboration of specialists in various fields, including pharmacology, medicine, biology, and bioinformatics. Fragmented, specialized algorithms and tools often address only narrow aspects of the overall problem. Heterogeneous, unstructured data landscapes require the expertise of specialized users. Hence, diverse data sources might not integrate smoothly across workflows.
papers.summary: ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that integrates disease module identification and drug repurposing prediction by coordinating specialized AI agents over heterogeneous biomedical data and networks. It aims to overcome the fragmentation of existing in silico tools by enabling natural-language-driven workflows that combine network analysis with expert-style reasoning. The platform is presented as a development study, with the abstract emphasizing the design rationale rather than reporting specific validated repurposing hits.

papers.title: Machine learning for RNA-small molecule interactions: methodologies, evaluation, and future directions.
papers.abstract: RNA is emerging as a compelling therapeutic target due to its rich structural diversity and central involvement in gene regulation, splicing, translation, and cellular signaling. Alongside advances in structural biology, computational approaches, especially machine learning and deep learning, have transformed the systematic analysis of RNA-small molecule interactions. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive survey of computational methods for RNA-small molecule interaction prediction, with a particular emphasis on three core tasks: binding site prediction, binding preference prediction, and
papers.summary: This review surveys machine learning and deep learning methods for predicting RNA-small molecule interactions, focusing on three core tasks: binding site prediction, binding preference prediction, and related interaction modeling. It organizes the computational landscape, discusses evaluation practices, and outlines future directions for RNA-targeted drug discovery.

papers.title: ADMET property prediction and toxicity profiling of CDK2 inhibitors: a practical cheminformatics tutorial using ADMET-AI 2.0 and RDKit.
papers.abstract: Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) prediction plays a central role in modern computer-aided drug discovery by enabling early evaluation of pharmacokinetic behaviour and safety liabilities. This tutorial presents a reproducible computational workflow for large-scale ADMET profiling using ADMET-AI 2.0, a graph neural network-based prediction platform, applied to 200 cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) inhibitors curated from ChEMBL release 35. Implemented within an annotated Jupyter notebook, the workflow integrates cheminformatics preprocessing, physicochemical p
papers.summary: This tutorial presents a reproducible Jupyter notebook workflow for large-scale ADMET profiling of 200 CDK2 inhibitors from ChEMBL, combining RDKit preprocessing with the ADMET-AI 2.0 graph neural network prediction platform. It demonstrates practical cheminformatics steps for evaluating pharmacokinetic behavior and toxicity liabilities in early drug discovery. The work is primarily educational, showing how to integrate existing tools rather than introducing new methods.

papers.title: Can AI Help Repurpose Drugs to Fight Against Antibiotic Resistance?
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing and development to meet the threat of antimicrobial resistance can be costly and time-consuming, but AI models may be able to help. In this News and Perspectives article, JMIR Correspondent Sara Novak reports on recent research training models to identify candidate drugs to treat resistant infections.
papers.summary: This news and perspectives article reports on recent research that trains AI models to identify candidate drugs for repurposing against antibiotic-resistant infections. It highlights how AI could speed up and reduce the cost of drug discovery in the fight against antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: Integrated experimental and computational study of a novel indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane as a potential inhibitor of Mcl-1.
papers.abstract: Myeloid cell leukemia-1 (Mcl-1) is a key anti-apoptotic protein that drives resistance to chemotherapy, making it a critical oncology target. In this study, we synthesized a new indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane via a one-pot multicomponent reaction and characterized its structure by FT-IR, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and mass spectrometry. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G (d) level were carried out to study its electronic features and reactive centers. In molecular docking against Mcl-1, the propellane derivative showed a binding score of -5.678 kcal mol-1, outperfor
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a novel indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane compound and characterized it spectroscopically, then used DFT calculations and molecular docking to assess its potential as an inhibitor of the anti-apoptotic protein Mcl-1, a cancer drug target. Docking suggested a modest binding affinity (-5.678 kcal/mol) that outperformed a comparator, but no experimental validation of Mcl-1 inhibition or cellular activity was reported.

papers.title: Utilising digital technologies for mycetoma management: A comprehensive review of advances and opportunities.
papers.abstract: Mycetoma is a neglected tropical disease characterised by chronic, destructive infections of subcutaneous tissues, predominantly affecting populations in endemic regions with limited healthcare resources. Delayed diagnosis, limited treatment options, and restricted access to specialised healthcare contribute to substantial morbidity, disability, and socioeconomic burden. Digital technologies offer promising opportunities to address these challenges and improve mycetoma care. Artificial intelligence (AI) can support early detection and diagnostic accuracy through the analysis of clinical images
papers.summary: This review examines how digital technologies, particularly artificial intelligence for analyzing clinical images, could improve the management of mycetoma, a neglected tropical disease causing chronic subcutaneous infections in resource-limited regions. The authors highlight opportunities for earlier detection and better diagnostic accuracy to address current delays in diagnosis and limited access to specialized care.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Novel Inhibitors of Escherichia coli MurB.
papers.abstract: MurB, a key enzyme involved in bacterial cell wall biosynthesis, represents a promising target for antibacterial drug discovery. In this study, a machine learning assay was employed to identify potential inhibitors targeting E. coli MurB. Five machine learning models were constructed using AutoMolDesigner, of which the RDKit_2D-based Model_2 was selected as the optimal activity-prediction model for virtual screening of an in-house compound library, yielding 238 compounds. These compounds were subsequently subjected to FRED molecular docking, and 16 candidate compounds were selected based on th
papers.summary: The authors built five machine-learning models to predict MurB inhibition and used the best one (RDKit 2D descriptors) to virtually screen an in-house library, yielding 238 hits that were narrowed to 16 candidates by molecular docking. The study demonstrates a computational pipeline for discovering antibacterial leads against E. coli MurB, though experimental validation of the candidates is not described in the abstract.

papers.title: A multimodal digital NeuroMarker platform with composite and domain-level validity for identification of mild cognitive impairment: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a clinically heterogeneous syndrome that can represent an early manifestation of neurodegenerative disease. Diagnosis relies on assessments that are difficult to scale, leaving many individuals unidentified.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study presents a multimodal digital NeuroMarker platform that combines multiple digital assessments to identify mild cognitive impairment, reporting both composite and domain-level validity. The approach aims to provide a scalable alternative to resource-intensive clinical assessments, potentially enabling broader identification of MCI in heterogeneous populations.

papers.title: Biosynthetic Pathways and Regulation of Antibacterial Compounds From Endophytic Fungi: From Chemistry to Genomics and Biotechnology.
papers.abstract: Endophytic fungi are non-pathogenic symbionts that represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive secondary metabolites. However, genome-mining studies reveal that most of their biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remain transcriptionally silent under standard laboratory conditions, leaving much of their chemical diversity unexplored. This review examines antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi by integrating three complementary aspects: metabolite chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and strategies for activating cryptic BGCs. Endophytic fungi produce polyketides, non-ribos
papers.summary: This review integrates the chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and genomic regulation of antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi. It highlights that most biosynthetic gene clusters in these fungi are silent under standard laboratory conditions, and surveys strategies for activating cryptic BGCs to access unexplored chemical diversity. The work connects metabolite chemistry with genomics and biotechnology to guide future antibacterial discovery.

papers.title: Interpretable Drug-Target Prediction via Geometric Alignment: A Linear Alternative to Deep Architectural Complexity.
papers.abstract: Designing selective kinase inhibitors is a multiobjective optimization problem constrained by the structural conservation of the human kinome, along with the lack of high-quality interaction data. Traditional deep learning methods often train complex neural networks directly on small datasets and fail to generalize to new chemical scaffolds. To this end, we present Geometric Manifold Alignment, a novel linear approach that shifts away from architectural complexity. We introduce Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), which aligns the latent spaces of ChemBERTa (small molecules) and ESM-2 (protein s
papers.summary: The authors propose Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), a linear method that aligns latent embeddings from ChemBERTa (for small molecules) and ESM-2 (for proteins) to predict kinase inhibitor–target interactions. By replacing complex deep architectures with geometric alignment, the approach aims to improve generalization to new chemical scaffolds despite limited interaction data. The work is framed as an interpretable alternative to deep learning for drug-target prediction.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.
papers.abstract: Animal behavior is a critical endpoint in preclinical pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutic discovery, yet conventional behavioral scoring remains labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and difficult to reproduce across laboratories. Artificial intelligence (AI) can now quantify behavior from video with greater spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution. This review summarizes how object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents are reshaping behavioral phenotyping. General-purpose object detectors rapidly lo
papers.summary: This review describes how AI methods—including object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents—are transforming animal behavioral phenotyping for preclinical pharmacology and therapeutic discovery. These approaches overcome the labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and poorly reproducible nature of conventional behavioral scoring by extracting richer spatial, temporal, and phenotypic information from video.

papers.title: UPLC-MS/MS-GNPS based metabolite profiling and inhibitory potential of Vitex negundo L. leaves against Shiga toxins: Applications for biodegradable films with antibacterial properties.
papers.abstract: Antibiotic therapy for STEC O157:H7 infections induces Shiga toxin release, highlighting the need for alternative, food-compatible antimicrobial strategies. The ethanolic leaf extract of Vitex negundo L. was characterized by UPLC-qTOF-MS/MS, integrated with Feature-Based Molecular Networking (GNPS), which putatively annotated 56 metabolites. Computational screening of all annotated compounds against the Stx1 and Stx2 B-subunits identified compound 8, an iridoid glycoside, as the top-ranked candidate with predicted Stx1-binding potential (ΔG = -6.9 kcal/mol; Ki = 8.7 µM). Over 100 ns of molecul
papers.summary: This study used UPLC-qTOF-MS/MS with GNPS molecular networking to annotate 56 metabolites from Vitex negundo leaf extract, then computationally screened them against Shiga toxin B-subunits, identifying an iridoid glycoside as a top Stx1-binding candidate. The work extends toward biodegradable antibacterial films for food safety against STEC O157:H7.

papers.title: SLC5A12 defines an invasive epithelial state associated with immune remodeling and therapeutic vulnerability in HNSCC.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by marked epithelial and immune heterogeneity. The malignant epithelial states associated with tumor progression, immune remodeling, and potential therapeutic vulnerability remain incompletely defined.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study identifies SLC5A12 as a marker of an invasive epithelial state in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). This state is linked to immune remodeling within the tumor microenvironment and points to a potential therapeutic vulnerability, suggesting SLC5A12 could help stratify patients or serve as a drug target.

papers.title: Design and validation of nucleosome binding peptides using BindCraft.
papers.abstract: Chromatin is a sophisticated assembly of DNA, RNA and proteins in the nuclei of eukaryotic cells. Protein-protein interactions that govern chromatin function are key regulators of genome activity, making them prime targets for drug discovery. Engineering and modulating these contacts presents a viable pathway for innovative epigenetic therapies. Nucleosomes, the primary structural units of chromatin, feature various interaction interfaces, most notably the acidic patch. This region serves as a critical binding site for numerous chromatin-associated proteins, often via their intrinsically disor
papers.summary: The authors used the BindCraft protein-design pipeline to computationally design short peptides that bind the nucleosome's acidic patch, a key chromatin protein-interaction interface. They then experimentally validated the designs, showing that de novo peptides can be engineered to target this epigenetic hub. The work demonstrates a proof-of-concept route toward peptide-based tools or therapeutics for modulating chromatin interactions.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Analysis Identifies Ion Channel-Related Biomarkers in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.abstract: Human ion channel genes (HICGs), as core effectors of transmembrane signal transduction, play a critical role in the initiation and progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the underlying mechanisms remain largely unclear. This study aimed to investigate the potential value of ion channel genes in COPD.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data to identify ion channel-related genes as potential biomarkers in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The authors highlight that human ion channel genes, which mediate transmembrane signaling, may play underappreciated roles in COPD onset and progression. The work nominates candidate ion channel biomarkers for further validation.

papers.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 meets artificial intelligence: a comprehensive review of AI-driven advances in drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (BMP4), a member of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily, plays pivotal roles in embryonic development, tissue homeostasis, and disease pathogenesis-including cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies over the past 5 years has created unprecedented opportunities for understanding and therapeutically targeting BMP4 biology at multiple scales, from atomic-resolution structure prediction to population-level clinical prognostication.
papers.summary: This review surveys how AI and machine learning are being applied to study and target BMP4, a TGF-β family signaling protein implicated in development, cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva. It covers AI-driven structure prediction, drug discovery efforts, and clinical translation, arguing that computational methods now enable BMP4 research across scales from atomic structure to population-level prognostication. As a review, it synthesizes rather than reports new primary findings.

papers.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
papers.abstract: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface.
papers.summary: This study identifies shared molecular features between diabetes and colorectal cancer, then tests whether the natural compound hupehenine can modulate these pathways. Using a diabetic-mimetic CRC model, the authors show that hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and alters macrophage marker profiles, suggesting a potential therapeutic axis at the diabetes–cancer interface.

papers.title: Virology-aware artificial intelligence for respiratory antiviral discovery: from molecular docking biases to RdRp-centered benchmarking.
papers.abstract: Respiratory RNA viruses remain a persistent threat because they combine high transmissibility, rapid evolution, immune escape, zoonotic spillover, and incomplete therapeutic coverage. RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps) and polymerase complexes are among the most conserved and pharmacologically actionable viral targets, yet they are also challenging computational targets because their ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, divalent metals, multidomain architecture, and conformational transitions. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), geometri
papers.summary: This review argues that AI-driven discovery of antivirals against respiratory RNA viruses must account for the complex biology of RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps), whose ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, metals, and conformational changes. The authors highlight biases in molecular docking and call for RdRp-centered benchmarking to make computational screening more virology-aware and reliable.

papers.title: Research progress on the application of multi-scale computational methods in the research and development of anti-tuberculosis infection drugs.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), driven by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of mortality from infectious disease worldwide.​ The global dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains-coupled with protracted treatment regimens and the persistence of latent infection-has not only compromised first-line chemotherapies but also underscored the stagnation of conventional drug development pipelines. In this review, we systematically synthesize how multi-scale computational strategies are reshaping anti-TB drug discovery and explicitly delineate the
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how multi-scale computational methods—spanning molecular modeling, network analysis, and systems-level approaches—are being applied to anti-tuberculosis drug discovery. It highlights how these strategies address the stagnation of conventional pipelines amid rising multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant Mtb strains. The paper frames computational integration as a route to accelerate target identification and drug development for TB.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic and computational analysis associates Ms4a6c+ macrophages with fibrosis in radiation proctitis and computationally nominates MOTS-c as a candidate modulator.
papers.abstract: Chronic radiation proctitis (CRP) represents a significant clinical challenge characterized by irreversible fibrosis and a lack of specific pharmacological interventions. This study aimed to elucidate the cellular mechanisms underlying impaired tissue repair to identify novel therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study combines transcriptomic profiling with computational analyses to identify Ms4a6c+ macrophages as a cell population associated with fibrosis in chronic radiation proctitis. The authors then use computational approaches to nominate MOTS-c as a candidate modulator of this fibrotic process. The work is exploratory and hypothesis-generating, with the therapeutic candidate identified in silico rather than validated experimentally.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and anti-cancer drugs: advancing discovery, personalization, and precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monit
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across the anticancer drug development pipeline, from target identification and virtual screening through molecular docking, pharmacokinetic prediction, and hit-to-lead optimization. It also discusses how machine learning can improve clinical trial design via patient stratification and enable real-time toxicity monitoring, addressing the long timelines, high costs, and patient heterogeneity that plague traditional oncology drug development.

papers.title: Cytochrome P450 inhibitors: friends or foes?
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes play a central role in the metabolism of xenobiotics and endogenous compounds, influencing drug pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety. Inhibition of these enzymes has traditionally been viewed as a major liability in drug discovery due to its association with drug-drug interactions (DDIs), toxicity, and metabolic instability. However, inhibition of specific CYP450 isoforms has emerged as a powerful therapeutic strategy in multiple disease areas, including cancer and infectious diseases. This review presents a comprehensive analysis of data and regulatory guida
papers.summary: This review argues that cytochrome P450 inhibitors, long considered a liability in drug discovery due to drug-drug interactions and toxicity, can also be exploited as therapeutic agents in cancer and infectious disease. It synthesizes data and regulatory guidance on both the risks and the therapeutic opportunities of isoform-specific CYP450 inhibition.

papers.title: Exploration or exploitation? The double-edged effects of AI use modes on radical creativity: evidence from AI-enabled drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely adopted in corporate innovation activities, yet prior research has not reached a consensus on whether it is more conducive to incremental or radical innovation. For radical innovation, which depends on highly novel ideas, realizing the value of AI depends not only on whether AI is adopted but, more importantly, on whether employees can use it creatively to transcend established knowledge boundaries. Drawing on environmental dynamism and the exploration-exploitation perspective, this study develops a theoretical model linking leaders' perceptions of
papers.summary: This study examines how different modes of AI use (exploration vs. exploitation) affect radical creativity in the context of AI-enabled drug discovery. Drawing on the exploration-exploitation framework and environmental dynamism, the authors propose a theoretical model linking leaders' perceptions to employee creative outcomes, arguing that AI's value for radical innovation depends on how creatively employees deploy it rather than mere adoption. The work is a conceptual/psychological model rather than an empirical bioinformatics study.

papers.title: Comparative multi-target computational profiling of ebelin lactone across cognition-associated proteins.
papers.abstract: Ebelin lactone (EL) is a bacoside-related triterpenoid derivative produced through acid hydrolysis and has previously shown binding affinity toward the M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors. However, its structural compatibility with proteins involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress responses, and neurite remodeling has not been systematically evaluated.
papers.summary: This study computationally screens ebelin lactone, a triterpenoid derived from bacosides, against multiple proteins linked to cognition, including targets involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress, and neurite remodeling. The work extends prior findings of its binding to M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors by profiling its structural compatibility across a broader set of cognition-associated proteins. It is an in silico docking/profiling study without experimental validation.

papers.title: Mapping the subcellular pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic landscape: a systems-pharmacology framework for predicting combination therapies against intracellular bacterial infections.
papers.abstract: Intracellular bacterial pathogens represent one of the most formidable challenges in contemporary medicine. By exploiting host cellular niches, these organisms evade immune surveillance and withstand conventional antibiotic therapies, establishing persistent reservoirs that are difficult to eradicate. Although antibiotic combinations, host-directed interventions, and drug repurposing have shown promise, conventional discovery pipelines rarely capture the dynamic and compartmentalized nature of the intracellular environment. This review proposes a systems pharmacology framework centered on subc
papers.summary: This review proposes a systems pharmacology framework that integrates subcellular pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics to predict how combination therapies will perform against intracellular bacterial infections. The authors argue that conventional drug discovery pipelines fail to account for the compartmentalized and dynamic nature of host-cell niches where pathogens persist, and that mapping drug exposure and effect at the subcellular level could improve rational design of antibiotic combinations and host-directed therapies.

papers.title: SCOPE-based target and pathway enrichment identifies the histamine H1 receptor as a regulator of exodosis.
papers.abstract: Phenotypic screening enables discovery of small molecules without requiring predefined targets, but mechanistic interpretation remains challenging due to polypharmacology and pathway complexity.
papers.summary: The authors apply a SCOPE-based enrichment approach to connect phenotypic screening hits to their targets and pathways, aiming to overcome challenges from polypharmacology. Using this method, they identify the histamine H1 receptor as a regulator of exodosis, a cellular process. The work demonstrates how computational target/pathway enrichment can extract mechanistic insight from phenotypic screens.

papers.title: Integrated in vitro and in silico assessment of antimicrobial, chemical antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities of endophytic Aspergillus sp. GK1 isolated from Mentha spicata roots.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are a source of structurally diverse endophytic fungi which harbor significant pharmaceutical potential.
papers.summary: The authors isolated an endophytic fungus, Aspergillus sp. GK1, from the roots of Mentha spicata and tested its extracts for antimicrobial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities using both laboratory assays and computational (in silico) methods. The study reports that the fungus produces compounds with measurable antimicrobial and antioxidant effects and shows some cytotoxicity, suggesting it may be a source of bioactive natural products. However, the findings are preliminary and based on crude extracts and computational predictions rather than purified compounds or mechanistic validation.

papers.title: An m5C-associated NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF programme marks melanoma cell states and immune features.
papers.abstract: RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C)-associated programmes may help characterise melanoma cell states and their immune context. We investigated an NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF (NYC) programme using patient-matched sequencing, experimental perturbation and multiscale transcriptomic analyses.
papers.summary: This study identifies an m5C RNA modification-associated programme involving NSUN5, YBX1, and CENPF (termed NYC) that characterises distinct melanoma cell states and correlates with immune features in patient tumours. Using patient-matched sequencing, perturbation experiments, and multiscale transcriptomic analyses, the authors link this programme to melanoma heterogeneity and immune context.

papers.title: Plasmid-Mediated AmpC Detection in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae: In Vitro Prevalence and In Silico Inhibitor Design.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the prevalence of AmpC beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae in clinical specimens collected in Lahore, Pakistan, and aimed to identify potential inhibitors targeting AmpC beta-lactamases.
papers.journal: The Canadian journal of infectious diseases & medical microbiology = Journal canadien des maladies infectieuses et de la microbiologie medicale
papers.summary: This study screened clinical isolates of E. coli and K. pneumoniae from Lahore, Pakistan, for plasmid-mediated AmpC beta-lactamase production, establishing local prevalence rates for these antibiotic-resistance enzymes. The authors then used computational (in silico) approaches to design or identify candidate inhibitor molecules targeting AmpC beta-lactamases. The work combines surveillance of resistance prevalence with early-stage computational drug discovery.
